config.title: Last Admission in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: How late you can still get into Berlin's main sights: last admission rules, the Museum Island weekday split, and what stays open into the evening.

items.q: What is the difference between closing time and last admission in Berlin?
items.a: **Closing time is when the building empties. Last admission is when the door stops accepting people.** At the Berliner Dom the gap is a full hour, at the Jewish Museum it is an hour (17:00 against an 18:00 close), and at Panoramapunkt the last lift goes up at 18:30 for a 19:00 close. Several venues publish only the closing time, so the cutoff is the number you have to go looking for.

items.q: Do all the Museum Island museums close at the same time?
items.a: **No, and this catches people out.** The Altes Museum and the Bode-Museum close at **17:00 from Tuesday to Friday** and at 18:00 at the weekend. The Neues Museum, the Alte Nationalgalerie and the James-Simon-Galerie close at **18:00** every day they open. All five are closed on Mondays, and the Pergamonmuseum is fully closed for reconstruction until 4 June 2027.

items.q: How late can I enter the Berliner Dom?
items.a: **One hour before it closes.** From 1 September to 31 May the Dom closes at 18:00 Monday to Friday and 17:00 on Saturday and Sunday, so the last entry is 17:00 on weekdays and **16:00 at the weekend**. Between 1 June and 31 August it stays open until 19:00 daily, which pushes the last entry to 18:00. The Dom recommends about an hour and a half inside, and the dome climb closes before the rest of the building.

items.q: What is still open in central Berlin after 18:00?
items.a: The **DDR Museum** runs to 21:00 every day of the year, the **TV Tower** to 23:00 on timed-slot tickets, **Topography of Terror** to 20:00 with free entry, and the **Reichstag dome** to midnight with a 21:45 last admission. The Reichstag is the only one of these you cannot decide on the spot: it needs advance online registration, or a confirmation collected at the service centre at least two hours before your slot.

items.q: Which day should I avoid for museums in Berlin?
items.a: **Monday** closes all five Museum Island buildings and the Jewish Museum. It is still a workable day, because the Humboldt Forum, the DDR Museum, the TV Tower, Topography of Terror, the Berliner Dom and the Reichstag all open. Watch the inversion though: the **Humboldt Forum closes on Tuesday**, so moving a Monday museum plan to Tuesday can swap one locked door for another.
